question: A conductor of length $0.50\text{ m}$ carries a current of $6\text{ A}$ along the positive $x$-direction. It is placed in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude $0.20\text{ T}$ along the positive $y$-direction. Obtain the vector expression for the force on the conductor and calculate its magnitude and direction. What change occurs if the magnetic field is reversed?

options.A: $\vec F=I(\vec B\times\vec l)=-0.60\hat k\,\text{N}$; reversing $\vec B$ leaves the force unchanged.
options.B: $\vec F=IlB\sin\theta=0.60\,\text{N}$ along the positive $y$-direction; reversing $\vec B$ makes the force zero.
options.C: $\vec F=I(\vec l\times\vec B)$. With $\vec l=0.50\hat i$ and $\vec B=0.20\hat j$, $\vec F=6(0.50\hat i\times0.20\hat j)=0.60\hat k\,\text{N}$. Reversing $\vec B$ reverses the force to $-0.60\hat k\,\text{N}$.
options.D: $\vec F=I(\vec l\cdot\vec B)=0.60\,\text{N}$ along the positive $z$-direction; reversing $\vec B$ doubles the force.
